claim: milled by mallet or tahona, fermented in stone, wood, clay or hide with the fibres present (and accept entry "ancestral keeps the fibres and uses clay pots")
because: NOM-070-SCFI-2016 section 4.4.3 (Mezcal Ancestral) allows milling "con mazo, tahona, molino chileno o egipcio", so the Chilean and Egyptian mills also qualify. For fermentation and distillation it says the process "puede incluir la fibra del maguey o agave (bagazo)": the fibres MAY be included, they are not required. The Artesanal class (4.4.2) uses the same "puede incluir" wording, so keeping the fibres does not set Ancestral apart. Ancestral differs from Artesanal in its pit oven only (no masonry oven), its mills (no trapiche or desgarradora) and its clay-pot distillation over direct fire (no copper).
fix: In ans, replace "milled by mallet or tahona, fermented in stone, wood, clay or hide with the fibres present" with "milled by mallet, tahona, or Chilean or Egyptian mill, fermented in stone, earth, trunk, masonry, wood, clay or hide (the fibres may be included)". In accept, replace "ancestral artesanal and plain mezcal ancestral keeps the fibres and uses clay pots" with "ancestral artesanal and plain mezcal ancestral uses pit ovens and clay pots".
